title: Fourier coefficient preserved on a subspace kernel
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements, and let $\gamma$ be a frequency with nonzero Fourier coefficient. If the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $f$ is less than $2^n$, then there exist a nonzero linear functional $\beta$ and a linear functional $\phi$ on its kernel such that the Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$ to that kernel at $\phi$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$.
